findings.title: A session's sign and inspect calls forcing governance off, so the one-time accounts' DRep key never signs: no test fails without it
findings.scenario: A site has a CIP-95 governance grant and is connected to a private session, and the session request JSON says "governance": true. Without the four overrides, cip30::keys_of (cip30.rs:466) adds the one-time accounts' DRep key Role::Drep 0. That key is the same for every session of account 24301, so it would sign the site's DRep certificate or vote. Every session that signs one is then linked by that key, and a DRep registration's deposit comes out of the session. No native test calls these four #[wasm_bindgen] wrappers: session_test.rs builds cip30::TxRequest itself with governance: false. The extension's tests reach the wrappers only through the prebuilt wasm/pkg, and none of them mentions a session's governance.
findings.since: 5969dd7a (2026-10-04, chunk 21, CIP-95), in web-wallet/1.6.0 (the first tag)
findings.evidence: In the copy, one mutant deleted the line `governance: false,` from inspect_session_tx (lib.rs:6453), sign_session_tx (:6465), session_data_signer (:6481) and sign_session_data (:6493). Ran session_test (14 passed, 1 ignored), cip30_test (73 passed), then the whole seedelf-wasm suite (16 targets, 305 passed). Nothing failed. A grep of extension/tests for governance (sessions.test.ts, sundae-orders.test.ts, order-cancel-check.test.ts, tx-view-screen.test.ts) found only tx-view-screen's public-account rows. A Rust mutant can't reach Vitest without rebuilding WebAssembly, so Vitest wasn't run.
findings.fix: Add a native test in session_test.rs that calls seedelf_wasm::sign_session_tx and inspect_session_tx; their Ok path needs no JavaScript. Pass a request JSON with "governance": true and a transaction carrying a vote or DRep certificate under account 24301's 3/0. Assert the summary treats that key as a stranger's and the witness set has no DRep signature. Do the same for session_data_signer with the DRep ID. Simpler still: move the override into one plain Rust function that all four call, and unit-test that function.
findings.known_check: Grepped docs/backlog.md, docs/archive/plans/ and docs/plans/ (excluding review-51) for 'governance: false', 'governance off' and session DRep. Only chunk-21-governance.md:153 states the rule (a design line, not a test). Nothing records this gap.

findings.title: A session's collateral never being a UTxO the evaluator refuses (L20): no test fails without it
findings.scenario: Anyone can send the session's address an ADA-only UTxO of exactly 5 ₳ (or the largest ADA-only one) that carries a reference script or a datum too deep to read. Without the filter, session_collateral can pick it as a merged return's collateral. Today plan_return's `evaluable` check (lib.rs:1184-1190) already turns any such row into a plain sweep, with no merge and no collateral, for both callers (lib.rs:1190 and :1478). So the filter is a second line that nothing reaches through session_return, and no test calls session_collateral directly.
findings.evidence: lib.rs:989 `.filter(|u| seedelf_core::eval::refusal(u).is_none());` replaced by `;`. Ran session_test (14 passed), then the whole seedelf-wasm suite (305 passed). Nothing failed.
findings.fix: Add a unit test in lib.rs's return_plan_tests. Over [a 5 ₳ ADA-only row with a reference script, a 3 ₳ plain row], session_collateral returns the 3 ₳ row. Over the refused row alone it returns None.
findings.known_check: Grepped backlog.md, archive/plans/ and plans/ for session_collateral, 'L20' and 'evaluator refuses': no record of a missing test.

findings.title: Several recipients (not a funding) being split into parts: no test fails without it
findings.scenario: The user sends Make public or Send to two addresses, or a transfer to two Seedelfs, and it needs more UTxOs than one transaction spends. With the guard the payment is refused. Without it, build_withdraw_parts and build_transfer_parts plan parts for payments[0] alone. Each part's request carries only the first payment: lib.rs:4747-4752 adds the others only to a funding's first part, and lib.rs:4621 builds a transfer part from payments[0]. The second recipient, named in the request, is never paid.
findings.since: 79742931 (2026-10-21) for :4793; 1cd50dba (2026-10-20) for the transfer's :4649; both in web-wallet/1.6.0
findings.evidence: Mutant 1: lib.rs:4793 `Err(e) if too_much(&e) && (request.payments.len() == 1 || funding) => e,` → `Err(e) if too_much(&e) => e,`. Mutant 2, the same class in transfers: lib.rs:4649 `Err(e) if too_much(&e) && request.payments.len() == 1 => e,` → `Err(e) if too_much(&e) => e,`. For each I ran api_test (92 passed), then the whole seedelf-wasm suite (305 passed). Nothing failed.
findings.fix: Add cases to api_test's parts_of_any_shape: two recipients over more UTxOs than one transaction spends, for example 30 UTxOs of 3 ₳ paying 40 ₳ to each of two addresses, and the same to two Seedelfs. build_withdraw_parts and build_transfer_parts must return Err, never Ok. Keep one case where a funding with its collateral beside still goes in parts. Fix both sites.

findings.title: An amount going out as more than MAX_PARTS (25) transactions: no test fails without it
findings.scenario: The user asks for an amount whose tokens sit in more UTxOs than 25 parts of 20 can spend, for example a pool's 520 boxes brought back, each holding a few of the token, all asked for. With the guard, in_parts refuses at part 25 with the first try's too-many error. Without it, the loop has no bound and plans as many parts as the tokens need. If it then falls back to a chain, `MAX_PARTS - 1 - anchor` (lib.rs:4220) underflows for any anchor past 24: a panic in a debug build, a wrap in release. Max has its own test of this limit (max_says_it_left_what_is_past_the_most_parts_a_payment_goes_as); amounts have none.
findings.evidence: lib.rs:4138 `if parts.len() + 1 >= MAX_PARTS {` → `if false && parts.len() + 1 >= MAX_PARTS {`. Ran api_test (92 passed), the whole seedelf-wasm suite (305 passed), and the ignored payment_parts_shapes_test in release (0 with problems, 108 refused, 0 of them Max). Every line's verdict and part count matched the baseline's. Nothing failed.
findings.fix: Add a unit test of in_parts with stand-in closures, so no proofs are built: 30×20+1 UTxOs, each holding one unit of a token, all of it asked for. Assert Err with the too-many error, and that `most`/`amount` are never called for a 25th part. A real build of 25 parts would be slow in debug.
findings.known_check: Grepped backlog.md and archive/plans/ for MAX_PARTS and 'more transactions than one payment'. chunk-34 records the limit; nothing records a missing amount test.

findings.title: The part sending the last tokens paying anything but exactly what's owed when its ADA covers it: no test fails without it
findings.scenario: A fitted part sends the last of the tokens, and its ADA covers what's still owed. This happens when the trailing try on what's left (lib.rs:4187) was too much for one transaction. The guard has that part pay exactly what's owed. Without it, keep = least([]) (lib.rs:4163) and the part pays what's owed less an ADA-only output's least. The loop then adds one more part paying that least (about 1 ₳) to the recipient, with its own fee, or refuses where nothing is left to pay it. This is traced, not observed: no api_test case and none of the 32 shapes reach this branch, and the shapes output did not change by a single line.
findings.evidence: lib.rs:4152 `if later.is_empty() && paid >= owed {` → `if false && later.is_empty() && paid >= owed {`. Ran api_test (92 passed) and the whole seedelf-wasm suite (305 passed). Then ran the ignored payment_parts_shapes_test in release: the full run hit the 30-minute cap after 30 of 32 shapes, with every line's verdict and part count matching the baseline's. The two shapes left, re-run alone with ONLY='A live: …' and ONLY='mixed x80', passed and matched the baseline too.
findings.fix: Add a unit test of in_parts with stand-in closures where the last part of tokens is fitted, the trailing try is too much, and the part's ADA covers what's owed. Assert it pays exactly that and that no part follows. Or build an api_test case that reaches the branch and check it with `none_after_paid`. One case covers #6 too.
findings.known_check: Grepped backlog.md and archive/plans/ for in_parts and 'pays exactly'. review-1.9.1.md (:32, :64, :87) covers reserving and the chained trailing part, not this branch.

findings.title: A part after the payment was paid in full, in parts that each pay their own fee: no test fails without it
findings.scenario: A fitted part itself finishes the payment: nothing owed, no token left. With the guard, in_parts returns. Without it, the loop goes on to `amount(rest, owed.max(least(&[])), [], false)` (lib.rs:4187-4192). That adds a part nobody asked for, paying the recipient an ADA-only output at its least (about 1 ₳) plus its fee, or refuses a payment already paid when nothing is left. It is in_parts' twin of #384's trailing part, which chained's owed == 0 check stops and chain_end_tests pins. The shapes suite's 'pays after the payment was all paid' check never fired, because no shape's fitted part finishes a payment. It is the same unreached branch as #5.
findings.evidence: lib.rs:4184 `if tokens.is_empty() && owed == 0 {` → `if false && tokens.is_empty() && owed == 0 {`. Ran api_test (92 passed), the whole seedelf-wasm suite (305 passed), and the ignored payment_parts_shapes_test in release, which completed within the cap (1558 s): 0 with problems, 108 refused, 0 of them Max, every line matching the baseline's. Nothing failed.
findings.fix: Add an in_parts unit test with stand-in closures, or an api_test parts case, in which the fitted part pays everything after the trailing try was too much. Assert no part follows (`none_after_paid`), as chain_end_tests does for a chain.

findings.title: A carry's amount being retried on the largest UTxOs: no test fails without it
findings.scenario: A chained part's carry (request.carry) must spend exactly the UTxOs it is given. When its picking is short at guessed budgets, the guard returns the shortfall, and fit_part tries fewer UTxOs. Without the `!request.carry` term, build_withdraw (and build_transfer at lib.rs:3172) measures the amount on the largest of the given UTxOs and builds a plain spend, not a carry. The part comes back with no carry, so next_of refuses the chain ('carries nothing forward') where fit_part's retry might have found a part. The funding half of the same guard is pinned; the carry half isn't.
findings.evidence: Mutant 1: lib.rs:3571 `if build::is_short(&short) && request.funding.is_none() && !request.carry =>` → `if build::is_short(&short) && request.funding.is_none() =>`. Mutant 2, the same class: lib.rs:3172 `Err(short) if build::is_short(&short) && !request.carry => {` → `Err(short) if build::is_short(&short) => {`. For each I ran api_test (92 passed), then the whole seedelf-wasm suite (305 passed). Nothing failed. Dropping the funding term instead fails says_the_most_an_amount_could_be_and_measures_one_the_guess_calls_short at api_test.rs:2387.
findings.fix: In says_the_most_an_amount_could_be_and_measures_one_the_guess_calls_short (api_test.rs:2341), add the carry case next to the funding one. With `carry: true` at `top - 5_000`, both build_withdraw and build_transfer must refuse with 'Not enough ADA in the Seedelf balance'.
findings.known_check: Grepped backlog.md and archive/plans/ for measured_or_more and is_short: 0 hits. chunk-34-token-pools.md:1125 describes `carry` but records no test of this guard.

findings.title: A chained part spending only its carry (a fee for nothing): no test fails without it
findings.scenario: In a chain, fit_part puts the carry first and adds picks from what's left (lib.rs:4060). When the picks come back empty, it builds a part over the carry alone, and next_of refuses that part ('spends nothing new'). Without the check, the chain accepts it: a fee for nothing and a little less carried forward each time, until `room` runs out (lib.rs:4270, :4570) or a later try ends the chain. It is rare: the picks come back empty beside a carry only when what's left holds nothing fit_part can add. Both chained and max_chained call next_of (lib.rs:4312 and :4594).
findings.evidence: lib.rs:4335 `if inputs_of(part).len() <= usize::from(forward.is_some()) {` → `if false && inputs_of(part).len() <= usize::from(forward.is_some()) {`. Ran api_test (92 passed), the whole seedelf-wasm suite (305 passed), and the ignored payment_parts_shapes_test in release (0 with problems, 108 refused, 0 of them Max, every line matching the baseline's). Nothing failed.
findings.fix: Add a unit test of next_of in lib.rs. A part whose only input is the forward carry gives Err 'spends nothing new'. A part that also spends one UTxO of its own gives Ok with its carry. One test covers both chain copies.
findings.known_check: Grepped backlog.md, archive/plans/ and plans/ for next_of, 'spends nothing new' and 'carries nothing forward': 0 hits.

findings.title: A second plan that takes as much as the first replacing it: no test fails without it
findings.scenario: reserving's second plan replaces the first only when it takes strictly less from the Seedelf balance. With `<=`, a second plan taking exactly as much, in no more parts or carries, replaces it. The total taken and the number of parts are the same; what can change is how the total splits between the payment and the fees, and which UTxOs each part spends. No test builds an equal pair. The two sibling conditions are pinned.
findings.evidence: lib.rs:4390 `&& takes(&again)? < takes(&first)? =>` → `&& takes(&again)? <= takes(&first)? =>`. Ran api_test's parts_of_any_shape (25 passed), then the whole seedelf-wasm suite (305 passed). Nothing failed. Dropping :4388 or :4389 instead fails a_second_plan_goes_only_in_no_more_parts_or_carries.
findings.fix: Add a unit test of reserving with stand-in parts where the second plan takes exactly as much as the first. Assert the first plan is kept.

findings.title: Re-planning a payment whose first plan pays no more than asked: no test fails without it
findings.scenario: reserving keeps the first plan when it pays no more than asked, or no more than its token parts' leasts. Without that early return it always plans again. The second plan is taken only where it takes strictly less in no more parts or carries (lib.rs:4388-4390, which tests pin), so the outcome can only stay the same or improve. The cost is a second planning, with every part built and proven again, on every payment in parts. I found no money effect: this guard saves time.
findings.evidence: lib.rs:4372 `if paid <= owed.max(leasts.iter().sum()) {` → `if false && paid <= owed.max(leasts.iter().sum()) {`. Ran api_test's parts_of_any_shape (25 passed), then the whole seedelf-wasm suite (305 passed). Nothing failed.
findings.fix: Add a unit test of reserving whose `plan` closure counts its calls. Over a first plan that pays exactly what was asked, it is called once.

findings.title: A carry read back from an output that isn't it (two outputs could be the carry): no test fails without it
findings.scenario: build::carried reads a chain part's carry as the one wallet-contract output holding rest_lovelace and no token, and refuses when two outputs could be it. Without that check, the first match wins. That can happen when a carry part with no tokens to send pays the Seedelf an ADA-only least (transfer_plan raises Some(0) to it, lib.rs:3048) and the rest carried equals that least to the lovelace. The recipient's output would then be read as the carry, and the next part would try to spend a UTxO this key doesn't own, which fails evaluation; for a payment to the user's own Seedelf, it would spend that payment instead. It needs an exact coincidence, so it is improbable.
findings.evidence: build.rs:2267 `if carries.next().is_some() {` → `if false && carries.next().is_some() {`. The lane gave 2264, which is the none case's `.context`. Ran api_test (92 passed), seedelf-core's whole suite (31 targets, 356 passed), and the whole seedelf-wasm suite (305 passed). Nothing failed. The CLI doesn't call `carried`.
findings.fix: Add a seedelf-core test (build_test.rs) that hands `carried` a FinalSpend whose transaction has two wallet-contract outputs of rest_lovelace with no token: Err 'two outputs that could carry its ADA forward'. Add one with no such output: Err 'no output carrying its ADA forward'.
findings.known_check: Grepped backlog.md and archive/plans/ for 'carried(' and 'two outputs that could carry'. Only chunk-34-token-pools.md:1124 describes `carried`; it records no test.

findings.title: A spent input with no key path being skipped, not refused, when the account signs: no test fails without it
findings.scenario: sign_with_paths signs once per payment key among the inputs spent, and refuses an input missing from `paths` ('no key path'). Without that refusal, the input's key is skipped and the transaction goes out short a witness, which the ledger refuses. Every caller builds `paths` with check_paths over the same rows it spends, so nothing reaches this today. The other half, signing with only the spent inputs' keys, is pinned.
findings.evidence: lib.rs:334-338 `let path = *paths.get(&(utxo.tx_hash.clone(), utxo.tx_index)).ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("no key path for UTxO {}#{}", ...))?;` → `let Some(&path) = paths.get(&(utxo.tx_hash.clone(), utxo.tx_index)) else { continue; };`. Ran api_test (92 passed), then the whole seedelf-wasm suite (305 passed). Nothing failed.
findings.fix: Add a unit test in lib.rs: sign_with_paths with a spent UTxO absent from `paths` returns an Err naming that UTxO.
findings.known_check: Grepped backlog.md and archive/plans/ for sign_with_paths and 'no key path': 0 hits.

findings.title: A return merging into more than MAX_MERGE (4) of the funding's UTxOs: no test fails without it
findings.scenario: merged_return refuses to merge into more than four funding changes; MERGED_OVERHEAD_BYTES (lib.rs:1059) prices a merged return for four at most. Without the check, a return with five or more would be built, priced below the plan's estimate, and only the network's size limit would catch it. The worker already slices the merge to four (sessions.ts:5049, its own MAX_MERGE at :793), so nothing reaches this today. The check_spendable half of the same guard is pinned (session_test.rs:366).
findings.evidence: lib.rs:1367 `if merge.len() > MAX_MERGE {` → `if false && merge.len() > MAX_MERGE {`. Ran session_test (14 passed), then the whole seedelf-wasm suite (305 passed). Nothing failed.
findings.fix: Add a session_test case: a return with five funding changes in `merge` returns Err 'at most 4 of the funding's UTxOs'.

findings.title: An order cancel's funds or collateral not at the session's account: no test fails without it
findings.scenario: build_order_cancel refuses any funds or collateral row whose payment key isn't the session's. Without that, a row from another session or the public account would be spent in a cancel that only this session's key signs. The ledger refuses it for a missing witness, and the built cancel ties that row to the session. The rows come from the worker's read of the session's own account, so nothing reaches this today.
findings.evidence: lib.rs:807 `if payment_key_of(&row.address, network_flag) != Some(session.payment) {` → `if false && payment_key_of(&row.address, network_flag) != Some(session.payment) {`. Ran session_test (14 passed), the lib's unit tests including dex_order_tests (7 passed), then the whole seedelf-wasm suite (305 passed). Nothing failed.
findings.fix: Add a case in dex_order_tests (lib.rs) or session_test: build_order_cancel for session 0's order with a funds row at session 1's address returns Err "isn't at the session's account". Do the same for the collateral.
